checks: The anchored formula yields attained finite slopes, continuous capacity, an attained q_z on each compact fiber, and nonempty compact U_z. A ball gives positive q_z on every positive-volume fiber, and the compatible-support result puts every maximizing mark of such a fiber in its interior.

If zero lies outside conv(U_z), this hull is compact in finite dimension and strict separation produces a unit v and a margin eta between zero and one. The open set of directions with u·v<-eta contains U_z. For 0<s<=r/2 the new threshold is below the old one by more than eta s. The slab in the old radius-r ball spans centered normal coordinates [-eta s,0); the cross-section radius is at least sqrt(r^2-(r/2)^2)>=r/2. In d=1 its length is eta s, with kappa_0=1.

For each fixed slope lowering the same threshold enlarges all fiber traces. On the anchor fiber the slope vanishes, so the positive slab gain is uniform in every finite slope and persists under the infimum. Compactness of the complementary direction set, when nonempty, yields a strictly positive gap at the old mark. Joint continuity keeps that gap for small s and the ball keeps the new mark admissible. The directional minimum strictly improves, a contradiction.

Carathéodory and inclusion minimality give 2<=k<=d+1 distinct unit normals with all coefficients positive. Any positive dependence on a proper subset would normalize to a convex combination of zero, contradicting minimality. A second independent kernel vector would allow a positive coefficient vector to move to the boundary of the nonnegative orthant and reduce support, so the relation also has the usual circuit uniqueness property. Attained slopes give genuine caps with mass q_z and all pass through the given mark. The weighted sum of their margins vanishes identically on the whole plane over z, so at least one closed margin is nonnegative at each point.

On a null site's minimal face all fibers are null. The pair with margins Tg(w)+u·y and Tg(w)-u·y has a common finite T large enough for strict exclusion at every off-face original fiber. Its restrictions at z are opposite closed halfspaces through the origin in continuous coordinates. Their masses are zero and 2<=d+1 even in d=1. Across all sites the count is at most |P|(d+1), and caps selected where q_z<Q have strict slack.

Exact low-dimensional spot check: P={0,1,2}, K_0={0}, K_1=[-1,1], K_2=[-2,2] is compatible. The mark 0 over site 1 has two caps with slopes -4 and normals ±1, excluding K_2 and each of mass 1. At site 2 the slopes 4 and normals ±1 exclude K_1 and each cap has mass 2. Centered interval lower bounds and the opposite-cap upper bounds give q_1=1 and q_2=2. The margins -3w±y at site 0 exclude both positive fibers, giving the null pair and strict slack at sites 0 and 1.
